I have farmed a long time, so I do not spread my land evenly just for appearance. I will keep cotton as my main crop because that is still the center of my system, and I have well irrigation, so I can support it properly. I will also keep maize and wheat on solid areas because they are dependable for grain and household security. I will leave smaller areas for millet and mungbean because they help me spread risk, use the land more flexibly, and fit the kind of mixed farming I trust. I am 65, so I will not choose an over-complicated plan or chase the highest-input path everywhere. I will use better seed where it clearly pays, keep fertilizer at a moderate working level, irrigate according to each crop’s real need, and use normal pest control rather than excessive spraying. For soil work, I will mostly use rotary tillage for convenience and labor saving, but I will keep ploughing for wheat land because I want a firmer base going into the winter season.
